chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn, and before him Ali ibn Abi Talib, and Muhammad ibn Ali and Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them all) said: How can we have knowledge of the future (hadith) in light of this verse: "Allah erases and confirms what He wills, and with Him is the Mother of the Book"?
"Allah erases and confirms what He wills, and with Him is the Mother of the Book."
As for one who says that the Almighty Allah does not know anything except after it comes into existence, he has become a disbeliever and has exited from monotheism.

key_terms.أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ: the Mother of the Book (Quran/Divine Record)

ai.seo_question: How do the Shia Imams reconcile their knowledge of the unseen with the Quranic verse about Allah erasing and confirming?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the theological defense of the Imams' pre-eternal knowledge (*ilm al-ghayb*) against the Jahmiyyah who denied it, using the verse of abrogation to distinguish between divine decree and actualization. It underscores the Shia position that the Imams' knowledge is intrinsic and not contingent upon the event's occurrence, thereby preserving the concept of *Tawhid* against those who limit God's knowledge to temporal events.
